Metadata.title: Dominik Huber | Full-Stack Developer
Metadata.description: Full-stack developer with a focus on UI/UX design, born in Ulm and at home in Cologne. I build fast, thoughtful web apps with Next.js, React and TypeScript.

HomePage.bio:
Hi, I'm Dominik, a full-stack developer with a focus on UI/UX design. I was born in Ulm, and today I'm at home in Cologne. I studied automotive and engine engineering, but somewhere between design and software engineering I found my real passion.

It all started in the sneaker scene. With JavaScript, HTML and CSS I built my first tools, which later helped more than 1,000 users buy limited releases. Small scripts turned into real products, and the question “How do I automate this?” more and more often became “How do I build this better?”

After that, I dug deeper into backend systems, APIs and scalable software, and eventually built ProfitPath together with fellow founders: my first big SaaS, made with <next>Next.js</next>, <react>React</react>, <ts>TypeScript</ts>, <go>Go</go> and <postgres>PostgreSQL</postgres>. Today, thousands of users rely on ProfitPath for access to more than 200 million product records, updated daily.
HomePage.bioAfterGraph: I love thoughtful interfaces, good interactions and the small details you don't consciously notice, but immediately miss when they're gone. That's exactly where my two worlds meet: I design with an engineer's understanding and build with a designer's eye.

story.p1: I probably spend more time in front of a screen than I'd like to admit. But at least it's usually for a good reason. I love writing code, turning new ideas into something real and building, step by step, a thought into something that actually works in the end. Most of the time, anyway.
story.p2: My interest in technology goes far beyond programming, though, especially when it comes to <apple>Apple</apple>. Since the iPhone 4, I've followed every new product with a mix of excitement and the question of whether I really need it. The answer is sitting in my living room: an entire sideboard full of Apple boxes. Throw them away? Unthinkable. They're well designed too.
story.p3: When I need a break from the screen, you'll often find me on the <golf>golf course</golf>. I like the mix of calm, focus and the fact that this sport regularly reminds you not to take yourself too seriously. Some days everything goes exactly as planned, and on others you're just happy to find your ball again. To clear my head on the other days, I also go running and hit the gym regularly. There, at least, you always know where the weight is.
story.p4: And then there's <latam>Latin America</latam>. Every trip there sparks my wanderlust, and I rarely come back without already planning the next one in my head. What impresses me most are the people: open, warm and with an ease that's contagious. You arrive as a stranger and an hour later you're sitting at the table with everyone. Back home it's Cumbia and Bachata, while I work, in the car and long after “just one song” has turned into the whole playlist.

TechStackPage.title: Tech stack
TechStackPage.description: The tools and technologies Dominik Huber works with: Next.js, React, TypeScript and more.
TechStackPage.intro: The tools I work with and the projects they're part of. It started with browser extensions in plain JavaScript; today it's platforms like ProfitPath, built with Next.js and TypeScript. Here you can see how well I know each tool and where I've used it.

nextjs.name: Next.js
nextjs.description: Server rendering, static pages, routing, data fetching and image optimization in one. ProfitPath is built on it, and so is this site.

react.name: React
react.description: The library for interfaces, in almost everything I build: web apps, extensions and, with React Native, mobile apps too.

reactNative.name: React Native & Expo
reactNative.description: We built the NexosSolutions app for Android and iOS with it, from one codebase for both platforms.

chromeExtensions.name: Chrome extensions & Webpack
chromeExtensions.description: Extensions built with React and bundled with Webpack: automated purchasing software, scrapers and small helpers that work where you already are.

typescript.name: TypeScript
typescript.description: Part of almost all my projects. Types make interfaces unambiguous, and many bugs show up while writing instead of in front of users.

javascript.name: JavaScript
javascript.description: NexosSolutions was a browser extension in plain JavaScript that automated selecting, buying and ordering limited items through web requests.

python.name: Python
python.description: My tool for scraping and data analysis. A university in Munich hired me for a project that collects data from the web for research and teaching.

go.name: Go
go.description: For backends where every millisecond counts. In some projects, a Go backend delivers the data to the frontend and answers the API requests.

nodejs.name: Node.js & Express
nodejs.description: The backend behind NexosSolutions: the API that supplied the extension and the app with data.

orpc.name: oRPC
orpc.description: Makes type-safe APIs almost effortless and fits right in with Next.js Server Actions and TanStack Query, which is why we use it in our projects.

tanstack.name: TanStack
tanstack.description: Query fetches the data, Table shows it, for example in ProfitPath's large tables. This site loads its data with TanStack Query as well.

postgresql.name: PostgreSQL
postgresql.description: My first choice for relational data. Supabase, which runs sign-in at ProfitPath, is built on PostgreSQL too.

mongodb.name: MongoDB
mongodb.description: NoSQL with JSON-like documents. At NexosSolutions it held the user and product data of the extension and the app.

supabase.name: Supabase
supabase.description: An open-source platform built on PostgreSQL. At ProfitPath, Supabase runs sign-in and keeps subscriptions in sync.

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.description: At ProfitPath, Stripe handles the payments and enables flexible payment options.

betterAuth.name: Better Auth
betterAuth.description: Self-hosted authentication without depending on a vendor. My choice when I want to keep authentication in my own hands.

profitpath.title: ProfitPath
profitpath.description: A platform for Amazon sellers. Finds profitable products for online arbitrage: supplier search, wholesale scanning, competitor analysis and automatic profit calculation, updated daily from the data of over 1,000 companies and suppliers.

profitgo.title: ProfitGo
profitgo.description: Product analysis on the go. The second product of the ProfitPath family: analyze products as soon as you visit a website or scan a barcode.

nexossolutions.title: NexosSolutions
nexossolutions.description: Automated purchasing software. A browser extension in plain JavaScript, HTML and CSS, plus an app for Android and iOS and its own API with a database behind it.

nexosproxies.title: NexosProxies
nexosproxies.description: A proxy network as a service. My own IP proxy network, first to cut my own costs, then as a service for others in the same situation.

portfolio.title: huberdominik.com
portfolio.description: My portfolio, the site you're on right now: bilingual without language URLs, text that streams in, a map with a driving car and a navigation written as a sentence.

CvPage.intro: My CV, read like a git log: the latest commit on top, the initial commit from 1997 at the very bottom. In between, a branch switch from automotive and engine technology to software, a few companies founded as forks of their own and today the main branch ProfitPath. Running since 1997 and far from finished.
